title: SFI protest over student suspensions, autonomous college norms turns violent in Thiruvananthapuram

ai.summary: SFI activists in Thiruvananthapuram protested against student suspensions at Sree Sankaracharya University and relaxed autonomous college norms, turning violent with clashes and banners targeting the Keralam Minister.

facts.claim: SFI protest over student suspensions, autonomous college norms turns violent in Thiruvananthapuram
facts.quote: SFI protest over student suspensions, autonomous college norms turns violent in Thiruvananthapuram

facts.claim: The march, led by Students' Federation of India state secretary P S Sanjeev, proceeded towards the Secretariat gate near the office of the state Higher Education minister.
facts.quote: The march, led by Students' Federation of India state secretary P S Sanjeev, proceeded towards the Secretariat gate near the office of the state Higher Education minister.

facts.claim: Despite police using water cannons four times to disperse the protesters, around 100 SFI activists refused to retreat, officials said.
facts.quote: Despite police using water cannons four times to disperse the protesters, around 100 SFI activists refused to retreat, officials said.

facts.claim: The protesters subsequently cut the ropes securing the barricades and attempted to move towards the Secretariat gate, they added.
facts.quote: The protesters subsequently cut the ropes securing the barricades and attempted to move towards the Secretariat gate, they added.

facts.claim: Police personnel were deployed in front of the gate to prevent the protesters from entering the Secretariat premises.
facts.quote: Police personnel were deployed in front of the gate to prevent the protesters from entering the Secretariat premises.

facts.claim: After being prevented from entering the compound, Sanjeev and some activists climbed onto a water cannon vehicle and put up a banner against the minister on top of it. Another banner was placed on the Secretariat compound wall.
facts.quote: After being prevented from entering the compound, Sanjeev and some activists climbed onto a water cannon vehicle and put up a banner against the minister on top of it. Another banner was placed on the Secretariat compound wall.

facts.claim: Sanjeev and other activists also addressed the protesters from atop the vehicle, police said.
facts.quote: Sanjeev and other activists also addressed the protesters from atop the vehicle, police said.

facts.claim: Officials said police personnel deployed at different gates of the Secretariat were unable to contain all the protest marches, allowing SFI activists to remove barricades at some locations.
facts.quote: Officials said police personnel deployed at different gates of the Secretariat were unable to contain all the protest marches, allowing SFI activists to remove barricades at some locations.

facts.claim: Police said a case would be registered against the protesters for allegedly damaging barricades and climbing onto the water cannon vehicle.
facts.quote: Police said a case would be registered against the protesters for allegedly damaging barricades and climbing onto the water cannon vehicle.

facts.claim: As many as 16 SFI-affiliated students of Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit in Kalady were suspended in August this year following protests against the vice-chancellor and the syndicate.
facts.quote: As many as 16 SFI-affiliated students of Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit in Kalady were suspended in August this year following protests against the vice-chancellor and the syndicate.

facts.claim: Subsequently, 10 students were denied permission to appear for examinations.
facts.quote: Subsequently, 10 students were denied permission to appear for examinations.

facts.claim: The protest was also against a recent Higher Education Department decision to do away with the requirement of prior government approval for autonomous colleges to introduce new self-financing courses and increase seats in existing programmes.
facts.quote: The protest was also against a recent Higher Education Department decision to do away with the requirement of prior government approval for autonomous colleges to introduce new self-financing courses and increase seats in existing programmes.

facts.claim: The decision has drawn criticism from Left parties, which alleged that it would allow autonomous aided and self-financing colleges to increase student intake without prior government approval, leading to the commercialisation of education and favouring private college managements.
facts.quote: The decision has drawn criticism from Left parties, which alleged that it would allow autonomous aided and self-financing colleges to increase student intake without prior government approval, leading to the commercialisation of education and favouring private college managements.
